extracted.intended_audience: Recording Academy members, recording artists, producers, engineers, record labels and other music industry professionals preparing GRAMMY submissions or credits
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and eligibility guidelines describing who is a nominee/recipient (statuette vs certificate), crediting thresholds (e.g., >50% playing time, 33% for multi-composer scores), role definitions, and which producer/engineer credits are eligible for GRAMMY statuettes across categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of Award Terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance of any award constitutes acceptance by the recipient (and successors) of all Recording Academy terms and conditions, including rules and policies adopted by the Board of Trustees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must furnish written acceptance when requested. Acceptance binds transferees and successors to the same terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statuette Use Restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Possession of a GRAMMY statuette is conditioned on use only for the recipient's personal, non-commercial purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any sale, auction, public exhibition, reproduction, or other public/commercial exploitation by recipient or third party without prior written consent of the Recording Academy is prohibited, null and void, and may trigger repossession of the statuette by the Academy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording Academy Reservation of Rights Over Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Academy may adopt rules/policies that make particular awards the property of the Recording Academy and reserve all rights (except right of possession as set forth), and require express written consent to sell/transfer/assign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such policies may be applied to particular awards or categories at the Board's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statuette Allocation — Individuals and Small Groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals and eligible members of groups of nine or fewer who are GRAMMY nominees on a winning project receive a GRAMMY statuette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to nominees listed as individuals or members of small groups (≤9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statuette/Certificate Allocation — Larger Groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Groups of 10 or more members receive one statuette engraved with the group/ensemble name sent to a designated group leader; individual group members are not GRAMMY winners (only the group is). For groups of 10–20 members, the Academy provides a special certificate and pin to each member and makes GRAMMY tickets available; for groups over 20, only the group leader is designated a nominee and no pins, certificates, tickets, or statuettes are available to group members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes statuette vs certificate/pin/ticket allocation by group size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Submission Process and Deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Recording Academy Voting and Professional Members may submit proposals to change GRAMMY rules, guidelines and definitions year-round; the cutoff date for proposals to be considered for the following year is March 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals are debated by the Awards & Nominations Committee, then the Board of Trustees. Rejected proposals are not reconsidered the next year except in special industry-change circumstances. Creating a new category requires a two-thirds supermajority of both committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producer & Engineer Eligibility Overview
rubrics_metrics.description: Producers and engineers receive GRAMMY statuettes in any Category where they are eligible to be nominated. For genre album categories, credited producers and engineers who have worked on greater than 50% of the playing time of a winning album receive a GRAMMY statuette; in these categories producers and engineers are not nominees and their eligibility is compiled and audited after the telecast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes that eligibility can be based on audited credits/playing time rather than nomination listings in certain album categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: 50% Playing Time Threshold for Album Category Statuettes
rubrics_metrics.description: For many album categories (e.g., Best Country Album, Best Reggae Album, etc.), Artist(s) of greater than 50% playing time on the album (and Artist(s) & Producer(s), Engineer/Mixer(s) of greater than 50% playing time if other than Artist(s)) receive statuettes; featured artists, producers & engineers with less than 50% playing time receive certificates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mastering Engineer(s), if other than Artist(s), and Immersive Producer(s)/Immersive Engineer/Mixer(s) may also be included per category rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Featured Contributors vs Principal Recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Featured Artist(s), Producer(s) & Engineer(s) with less than 50% playing time receive certificates (not statuettes) in album categories where the >50% rule applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificates indicate contribution but not statuette recipient status; mastery engineer and immersive credits may be treated separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Songwriting Eligibility — New Material Only
rubrics_metrics.description: For songwriting categories (e.g., Rap Song, Rap Songwriter(s)), only Songwriter(s) of new material are eligible to receive awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where sampled or interpolated material is used, Publishers & Songwriter(s) of sampled or interpolated material are credited/eligible 'if applicable'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher/Sampled Material Credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers and songwriters of sampled or interpolated material are credited and may be eligible where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to categories where sampled/interpolated portions are part of the nominated work; inclusion depends on presence of sampled/interpolated material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composer Minimum Playing Time for Multi-Composer Scores (33%)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Score Soundtrack for Video Games and Other Interactive Media, where more than one composer is listed a minimum of 33% playing time is required for a composer to be eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 33% playing time threshold also applies to Music Producer(s) & Engineer/Mixer(s) when more than one composer/production team is listed; certificates may be given to composers/producers/engineers below the threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music For Visual Media — Pre-Existing vs Newly Recorded Material Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For compilation soundtrack albums consisting largely of pre-existing masters, up to two album Producers and up to two Music Supervisors may be eligible; for albums consisting largely of new recordings, awards go to Principal Artist(s) with significant contributing performance(s), up to three Producer(s) (in extraordinary cases a fourth via appeal), and up to two Music Supervisors; Engineer/Mixer(s) of greater than 50% playing time of newly recorded material are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In absence of principal artists/in-studio producers, award to individuals proactively responsible for concept and musical direction and selection of artists/songs/producers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Musical Theater Album — Composer/Lyricist and Principal Vocalist Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Lyricist(s) & Composer(s) are eligible if they have written/composed a score that comprises greater than 50% playing time of the album and has not been previously nominated; up to four Principal Vocalist(s) with significant contributing performances (lead/featured vocalists) are eligible. Certificates are issued for vocalists in 'ensemble-driven pieces.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines 'significant contributing performance' as a lead performance by a featured vocalist and distinguishes ensemble-driven pieces from principal/chorus structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jazz/Large Ensemble Recipient Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For Jazz Performance: Artist(s) receive the award; for a Large Ensemble track the Group Leader and Group Members are recipients if the group is under 10. If the group is over 20, the sole statuette recipient will be the leader. If the group is 10–20, the Academy provides a special certificate and pin to each member of the group; GRAMMY tickets are made available to group members even though they are not nominees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies statuette vs certificate allocation by ensemble size and special-case ticketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producer Definition and Duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The producer is the primary person(s) contracted by and accountable to the content owner for delivering the recording as a finished product; the producer directs and has overall creative and technical oversight during the recording project and individual recording sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duties include overseeing sessions, making creative/technical/aesthetic decisions, choosing final takes/versions, participating in song selection, selecting musicians/engineers/studios, assigning and supplying accurate credits, managing budgets/schedules, and supervising mixing/mastering/quality control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible Producer Credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Credits considered eligible for producer statuettes include: Producer, Co-Producer (shares significant responsibilities/contributions), Vocal Production/Vocals Produced By (controls vocal recording), Compilation Producer (principal producer for compilation/historical categories only), and Immersive Audio Producer (same as producer for immersive audio).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Co-Producer must make significant and consequential contributions to be eligible; Compilation Producer eligible only in specified categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-Eligible Producer Credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Credits not eligible for producer statuettes include: Executive Producer (often label rep/funding person), Assistant Producer/Associate Producer/Additional Production (delegated/reporting roles), 'Strings (or Any Other Instrument) Produced By' (works on individual elements not overall production), and 'Produced on Behalf of (the Content Owner)' (appointed by content owner, more like exec/A&R).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These credits denote roles that do not constitute primary production responsibility for statuette eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engineer Definition and Duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The engineer is the primary person(s) actively responsible for the creative process of recording and/or mixing a project as well as technical decisions; operates or oversees equipment during recording and makes creative, technical and aesthetic choices in collaboration with the artist and producer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engineer responsibilities span both technical operation and creative sound decisions across recording and mixing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible Engineer Credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible engineer credits include: Engineer; Recording Engineer/Recorded By (not involved in final mixing); Mixed By/Mixer/Mix Engineer (creates mixdown for mastering); Remix Engineer/Remixer (Best Remixed Recording category only); Vocals Recorded/Engineered By; Balance Engineer (classical); Mastering Engineer (eligible only in specified categories like Record Of The Year, Best Engineered Album, etc.); Tonmeister (classical credit requiring graduation from official Tonmeister program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mastering Engineer eligibility is limited to named categories. Tonmeister must meet education prerequisites to use the title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engineered Album Categories — Eligible Engineers & Mastering Engineers
rubrics_metrics.description: For Engineered Album, Non-Classical and Engineered Album, Classical categories, Engineers (per P&E eligible credits list) and Mastering Engineer are the statuette recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: P&E list dictates eligible credits; these categories specifically award engineers and mastering engineers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical Album Recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: For Historical Album the statuette recipients include Compilation Producer(s), Restoration Engineer(s) & Mastering Engineer(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original recording producers/engineers and producers/engineers of under 50% playing time may be recognized per detailed criteria; no certificates issued for Historical Album in some instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music Video/Film Recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: For Music Video and Music Film categories, Artist(s), Video Director(s) & Video Producer(s) are primary recipients; Audio Producer(s), Audio Mixer & Video Editor may be recipients depending on percentage of music/video playing time (over or under 51%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artist(s), Video Director & Video Producer(s) of over 51% of total playing time of music video are statuette recipients; those with less than thresholds may receive certificates per category rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immersive Audio Album Credits
rubrics_metrics.description: For Immersive Audio Album categories, IA Engineer, IA Producer & IA Mastering Engineer are the credited recipients; if album is released only in multichannel format the Producer(s) and Engineer(s) receive an award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immersive-specific production and engineering roles are explicitly recognized and treated similarly to standard producer/engineer roles but with immersive designation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composing/Arranging Category Recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Instrumental Composition awards go to Composer(s); Arrangement awards go to Arranger(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No certificates are issued for some composing/arranging categories; publisher credits may be relevant for publishing awards.
